interpretation: The complete static cellwise representation A/B/M/G plus a continuous marginal score vector was exactly identical across four topology worlds in every replicate.
Despite that static equivalence, pairwise occurrence relations, first-passage depths and single-node intervention responses differed in every replicate.
For 10 active nodes the chain and star worlds differed in 36 ordered-pair reachability entries on average; for 14 active nodes the difference rose to 78.

Single-node knockout robustness differed strongly despite identical M masks: at 14 active nodes the chain retained 0.538 of remaining active nodes on average while star and redundant worlds retained 1.0.
The BAM accessibility mask records which nodes are reachable from the source, but not how that accessibility is organized internally.
A nodewise marginal/raster representation is therefore insufficient for topology-sensitive questions even under complete occurrence-map knowledge.
claim_boundary: The generic fact that equal marginals need not determine joint/topological structure is not claimed as new mathematics.
The ecological contribution is to show exactly which EOG distribution-history targets are discarded by a nodewise BAM/raster representation in controlled known-truth worlds.
The controlled chain/star/tree/redundant topologies are experimental archetypes rather than estimates of real dispersal networks.
This result does not by itself establish predictive superiority over empirical SDMs.
